title: The Earth's Atmosphere and Greenhouse Effect

flashcard_questions.q: The layer of gases surrounding the Earth, currently made up of roughly 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and small amounts of other gases.
The release of gases from the interior of the Earth through volcanic eruptions. Volcanic degassing released carbon dioxide, water vapour, nitrogen, and other gases that formed the early atmosphere.

The process by which plants and algae use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose and oxygen. Photosynthesis is responsible for the increase in atmospheric oxygen over billions of years.
Which planet, along with Venus, still has an atmosphere that is mostly carbon dioxide?

flashcard_questions.a: A natural process where gases in the air absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, keeping the Earth warm.
